summary: Same 16-column rainbow bouncing-bar pattern and an essentially exact match once MotionSensitivity is dialed to 0, but at default (and at MotionSensitivity 0.5/1) the port's accelerometer path suppresses the audio-driven bounce entirely: it decays to near-black for ~2-3 s out of every ~9 s and averages about half the original's brightness, while the original bounces continuously on a rock-steady ~1.05 s cycle.
observations: Rig: default 16x16 grid, 256 px. Both sides compile and run clean (no compile/runtime errors) and both report wantsSensors:true, so both were fed the beat120 synthetic feed on every run below unless stated.

Shared look: 16 vertical bars, one per grid column, each rising from the bottom to a per-column height; the fill is a rainbow ramp by row (red at the top through violet at the bottom) and a bright white cap row sits on top of each bar. ShowRainbow=0 strips the rainbow and leaves only the white cap row. Same drawing on both sides.

Control surface matches exactly: both sides expose sliderGravity (Gravity), sliderMotionSensitivity (MotionSensitivity), sliderShowRainbow (ShowRainbow), sliderRandomness (Randomness), all kind 'slider'.

HEADLINE, untouched defaults, 60 s survey @10 fps: original meanBrightness 83, motion 61, brightnessTrend steady; port meanBrightness 45, motion 32, brightnessTrend decaying. The port is ~45% dimmer and ~48% less active.

Original's temporal structure is a single regime for the whole 60 s: autocorrelation of meanBrightness peaks at 1.10 s (@10 fps) / 1.05 s (@20 fps) / 1.02 s (@40 fps) with r=0.99-1.00 at every harmonic out to 15 s. Its rhythm image (survey, late-20, late-45) is uniform horizontal banding with no long-period envelope at all; amplitude never sags.

Port's temporal structure at defaults has a second, much slower regime the original does not have: on top of a ~0.80-0.90 s bounce it runs an ~8.8 s (@20 fps) / ~9.3 s (@10 fps) decay-and-relaunch super-cycle, r=0.96-0.98. Binned 1-s meanBrightness over the survey reads 90 69 62 56 38 30 22 19 16 -> 70 79 63 50 45 33 25 20 16 -> ... i.e. bars fade over ~7 s to essentially black (mean 16 = the floor) and hold there ~2-3 s before snapping back to full.

The dead stretch is plainly visible as a solid black band across the port's rhythm image in the late-20 run (t~25-28 s) and as near-black contact-sheet cells at 16.2 s and 54.5 s in the survey; the original's rhythm image over the same window is unbroken banding.

Cause is localized to the MotionSensitivity/accelerometer path. With sliderMotionSensitivity=0 set on BOTH sides (30 s @10 fps): original mean 83 / motion 62, port mean 83 / motion 61, and the port's autocorrelation becomes 1.10 s at r=0.99-1.00 with every harmonic matching the original's - the ~9 s super-cycle disappears completely. With sliderMotionSensitivity=1 on both sides: original still 83/62 (unchanged), port drops back to 46/32 with the 9.3 s super-cycle.

The original's MotionSensitivity slider is genuinely inert on output: probe deltas 0.00 at all of 0, 0.5, 1 over a 12 s window, and manual 30 s sweeps at 0 and 1 give byte-identical summary stats (83/62 both). The port's is strongly live (probe delta 87.97 at 0). So this is a case of the port HAVING an effect the original does not, not a missing dial.

Both sides do depend on the sensor feed for their energy, so this is not the port ignoring sensors: with --sensors off the original collapses to mean 25 / motion 9 (weak, r=0.66 at 0.90 s) while the port sits at mean 46 / motion 32 - and with --sensors off the port's MotionSensitivity=0 no longer helps (still 46/32), showing the port's broken state is what happens when its accelerometer term is allowed to override the audio-driven launch.

Ball-height spread (secondary, measured with MotionSensitivity=0 on both, 32 dumps across 12 s @20 fps, top lit row per column): original max-minus-min across the 16 columns averages 1.75 rows (max 3); port averages 3.00 rows (max 6). The port's bars fan out roughly 1.7x wider than the original's, which is why ShowRainbow=0 draws a nearly solid white line on the original and a visibly dashed/broken line on the port.

Per-column colour texture differs slightly: the original's rhythm image shows 3-4 broad, stable column regions of differing mean tint held for the whole 30-60 s window; the port's varies column-to-column on a finer scale. Same palette family (full rainbow ramp), same saturation and brightness range (both 16..136 min/max in the 6 s baseline).

No frame-rate coupling on either side: the original's cycle measures 1.10 / 1.05 / 1.02 s at 10 / 20 / 40 fps and the port's 0.90 / 0.80 / 0.80 s - both essentially fps-invariant (the small drift is frame quantization), so the period difference at defaults is a real behavioural difference, not a sampling artefact.
Seed 7 reproduces the defaults divergence exactly (orig 83/62 steady; port 46/32 with the 9.3 s super-cycle), so it is not a one-seed fluke.

dials.name: sliderGravity
dials.origEffect: Raises activity monotonically: motion stat 52 -> 56 -> 63 -> 81 -> 83 -> 86 -> 87 -> 88 -> 86 across g = 0, 0.1, 0.25, 0.4, 0.5, 0.6, 0.75, 0.9, 1 (20 s @10 fps, MotionSensitivity pinned to 0). Bars snap up and fall back harder as g rises; the ~1.1 s cycle length itself does not change.
dials.portEffect: Same monotonic direction and the same unchanged ~1.1 s cycle, but the curve is shifted: motion 40 -> 46 -> 50 -> 60 -> 62 -> 68 -> 83 -> 85 -> 84 over the same values. The port only reaches the original's activity level at g >= 0.75; at g = 0.4-0.5 it is ~25% less active while being brighter (mean 98/89 vs the original's 85/80).

dials.name: sliderMotionSensitivity
dials.origEffect: No effect on output at any value. Probe delta 0.00 at 0/0.5/1 over 12 s; manual 30 s runs at 0 and at 1 both give mean 83 / motion 62 with an identical 1.10 s autocorrelation. Dial effect unverifiable from output on the original.
dials.portEffect: Dominant and destructive. At 0 the port matches the original (mean 83 / motion 61, 1.10 s cycle). At 0.5, 1 and untouched-default it falls into the ~9 s decay-and-relaunch mode (mean 46 / motion 32) with multi-second black gaps, i.e. the accelerometer term overrides the audio-driven bounce instead of modulating it.

dials.name: sliderShowRainbow
dials.origEffect: Binary. At 0, 0.1 and 0.4 the rainbow fill is off and only the white cap row is drawn (mean 16 / motion 23). At 0.5, 0.6, 0.9 and 1 the rainbow fill is on (mean 82-83 / motion 61). Switch point is at or below 0.5, i.e. 0.5 counts as ON.
dials.portEffect: Identical binary behaviour and identical stats on both sides of the switch (off: 16/23; on: 82-83/61), with one boundary difference: at exactly 0.5 the port is OFF (16/23) where the original is ON (83/61). Everywhere else - 0, 0.1, 0.4, 0.6, 0.9, 1 - the two agree exactly.

dials.name: sliderRandomness
dials.origEffect: Adds jitter and slightly damps the pattern: mean/motion 87/64 at 0, 83/62 at 0.5, 79/57 at 1 (30 s @10 fps, MotionSensitivity 0). The 1.1 s autocorrelation degrades from r=0.97 at 0 to r=0.95 at 1 as the bars desynchronise.
dials.portEffect: Same values to within a point at every setting: 87/64 at 0, 83/61 at 0.5, 79/57 at 1, with the same r=1.00 -> 0.96 autocorrelation decay. Exact match.

feedback: The whole verdict turns on one thing: the port's MotionSensitivity/accelerometer contribution must not be able to override the sensor-driven bounce. With MotionSensitivity dialed to 0 the port is already an excellent match to the original (mean 83 vs 83, motion 61 vs 62, identical 1.10 s autocorrelation with matching harmonics out to 15 s). Fix the accelerometer path and the pattern is essentially done.

Concretely: at default dials the port's mean brightness must go from ~45 to ~83 and its brightnessTrend from 'decaying' to 'steady'. The original's meanBrightness never sags below its 1.1 s cycle floor over 60 s; the port currently fades to the black floor (16) for ~2-3 s out of every ~9 s. There must be NO ~9 s super-cycle - the original's autocorrelation has peaks only at multiples of ~1.05 s, nothing near 8-10 s.

The original's MotionSensitivity slider produces zero output change at 0, 0.5 and 1 under the standard synthetic accelerometer feed (an 8 s tilt circle of radius 0.2 about a constant z). Whatever gate or threshold makes the original ignore a tilt of that magnitude is missing from the port - the port reacts strongly to it. Keep the control on the surface (it is in the original's control list) but make its output response match, i.e. no visible change across 0/0.5/1 for a tilt of this size.

Gravity response is mis-scaled in the low and middle of its range. Measured with MotionSensitivity=0 over 20 s @10 fps, the original's motion stat is 52/63/83/87 at g = 0/0.25/0.5/0.75 while the port posts 40/50/62/83 - the port needs roughly g+0.25 to reach the original's activity. Steepen the port's low/mid gravity response so g=0.5 lands near motion 83, not 62; the top end (g >= 0.75) already agrees.

The port's balls fan out too far. With the same dials, the vertical spread between the highest and lowest column top averages 1.75 rows on a 16-row grid for the original (never more than 3) but 3.00 rows for the port (up to 6). Tighten the per-ball phase/height variation by roughly a factor of 1.7 - the visible tell is ShowRainbow=0, where the original's white cap row reads as one nearly unbroken line across all 16 columns and the port's reads as a dashed, broken line.

Nitpick only: ShowRainbow's on/off boundary is off by one comparison. The original treats exactly 0.5 as ON, the port treats it as OFF; 0, 0.1, 0.4, 0.6, 0.9 and 1 all agree. Make the port's test inclusive at 0.5.

Minor colour/texture note: the original holds 3-4 broad, stable column regions of differing mean tint for the whole window, while the port's per-column tint varies on a finer column-to-column scale. Same palette family and same 16..136 brightness range, so this is low priority behind the items above.
